question: According to the data, what is the daily free-episode limit for free users, and has it changed during 2026?

name: run_sql
purpose: Checks the observed view-type and content-tier combinations by month, including repeat-view volume, to identify which events can reveal the free-user daily episode cap.
query: SELECT cv.view_type, cc.content_tier, substr(cv.date,1,7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS view_rows, COUNT(DISTINCT cv.user_id || ':' || cv.date) AS user_days, COUNT(DISTINCT cv.user_id || ':' || cv.date || ':' || cv.content_id || ':' || cv.episode_number) AS distinct_episode_user_days, MAX(cv.episode_number) AS max_episode_number FROM content_views cv JOIN content_catalog cc ON cc.content_id=cv.content_id GROUP BY cv.view_type, cc.content_tier, month ORDER BY month, cv.view_type, cc.content_tier

name: update_hypotheses

hypotheses.statement: The daily free-episode allowance is consistently eight, as stated in the product brief.
hypotheses.evidence: The event schema has no configuration or policy-history table; April–September view logs show free views of free-tier content, but per-user-day counts have not yet been summarized.

hypotheses.statement: The limit changed during 2026, and the change is visible as a shift in users' daily free-view counts.
hypotheses.evidence: Not yet tested; observed view events start April 2026.

hypotheses.statement: Observed counts could differ from the configured limit because many users stop before reaching it, so view logs alone may not establish the policy.
hypotheses.evidence: Need to check monthly per-user-day counts for concentration at an apparent ceiling and identify any periods where users exceed eight.

next_step: Summarize unique free-tier episode views per user-day by month, including the maximum and counts around eight, to see whether the logs support a stable or changed cap.

name: run_sql
purpose: Tests whether free-tier viewing has a monthly ceiling at eight or a shift in the observed per-user-day maximum.
query: WITH daily AS (SELECT substr(date,1,7) AS month, date, user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT content_id || ':' || episode_number) AS free_episodes FROM content_views WHERE view_type='free' GROUP BY month,date,user_id) SELECT month, COUNT(*) AS user_days, SUM(CASE WHEN free_episodes=8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS exactly_8, SUM(CASE WHEN free_episodes>8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS over_8, SUM(CASE WHEN free_episodes>=7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS at_least_7, MAX(free_episodes) AS max_per_user_day, ROUND(AVG(free_episodes),2) AS avg_per_user_day FROM daily GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

name: run_sql
purpose: Pins down the timing of the apparent daily cap change by checking the maximum per-user free-episode count on each date.
query: WITH daily AS (SELECT date, user_id, COUNT(DISTINCT content_id || ':' || episode_number) AS free_episodes FROM content_views WHERE view_type='free' GROUP BY date,user_id), daymax AS (SELECT date, MAX(free_episodes) AS max_user_day FROM daily GROUP BY date) SELECT substr(date,1,7) AS month, MIN(date) AS first_date, MAX(date) AS last_date, COUNT(*) AS calendar_days, SUM(CASE WHEN max_user_day=5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS days_max_5, SUM(CASE WHEN max_user_day=8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS days_max_8, MIN(CASE WHEN max_user_day=8 THEN date END) AS first_date_max_8, MAX(CASE WHEN max_user_day=5 THEN date END) AS last_date_max_5, MAX(max_user_day) AS monthly_max FROM daymax GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

name: update_hypotheses

hypotheses.statement: The daily free-episode allowance is consistently eight, as stated in the product brief.
hypotheses.evidence: Observed free-tier free-view maxima are exactly 5 on every observed date in April–June 2026, and exactly 8 on every observed date in July–September 2026.

hypotheses.statement: The limit changed during 2026, and the change is visible as a shift in users' daily free-view counts.
hypotheses.evidence: All 91 observed dates from April 1 through June 30 had a daily maximum of 5; all 92 dates from July 1 through September 30 had a maximum of 8. No user-day exceeded the monthly maximum.

hypotheses.statement: Observed counts could differ from the configured limit because many users stop before reaching it, so view logs alone may not establish the policy.
hypotheses.evidence: Monthly average episodes per user-day were only 2.82–3.22, well below the observed ceiling; event logs indicate an effective ceiling but contain no policy/configuration history.

next_step: Respond with the observed effective caps and timing, explicitly caveating that the database contains view events rather than policy configuration and only covers April–September 2026.

answer:
## Answer
The viewing data shows an effective daily free-episode ceiling of **5 episodes from April through June 2026**, rising to **8 episodes from July through September**. So, yes—the observed limit changed during 2026, apparently on **July 1**.

## Definition and scope
I counted distinct free-tier episodes watched with `view_type = free` per user per day. View data covers **April 1–September 30, 2026**.

## Data quality
The database records viewing events, not the configured limit or its change history. The observed maximum was 5 on every date in April–June and 8 on every date in July–September; no user-day exceeded its period’s maximum. This supports an effective-limit change, but does not independently confirm the policy setting or its exact implementation date.
